name: ADV7611BSWZ
title: ADV7611: single-input low-power 165 MHz HDMI 1.4a receiver with 24-bit video output, 64-lead LQFP_EP
summary: The ADV7611 takes one HDMI 1.4a input and delivers decoded video on a 24-bit parallel output bus with HS, VS/FIELD, DE and a line-locked clock, plus extracted audio as I2S or S/PDIF. It handles TMDS clocks up to 165 MHz (formats up to UXGA 60 Hz at 8 bit), decrypts HDCP 1.4 with keys held on chip, supports repeaters up to 127 KSVs, and includes a programmable cable equalizer, EDID RAM, a CEC controller and a 3 × 3 colour space converter. It runs from 1.8 V and 3.3 V rails, is configured over I2C, and comes in a 10 mm × 10 mm 64-lead LQFP_EP rated −40°C to +85°C, in standard, non-HDCP and automotive (W) versions.
key_figures: 165 MHz max (UXGA 60 Hz at 8 bit, 162.5 MHz)
24-bit, SDR or DDR; LLC 13.5 MHz to 165 MHz
HDCP 1.4, internal keys; repeater up to 127 KSVs
DVDD, PVDD, CVDD 1.71 V to 1.89 V; DVDDIO, TVDD 3.14 V to 3.46 V
I2C, 400 kHz; main map 0x98 after reset

notes: Z marks a RoHS-compliant part; W marks a part qualified for automotive use; -P is the version without HDCP; -RL is a 13-inch reel.
Only the W models are for automotive applications, and their specifications may differ from the other models.

operation.text: Sold in automotive, professional (without HDCP) and industrial versions, all rated −40°C to +85°C. Register-level detail lives in the companion user guide UG-180, which is required to use the part.

One HDMI-capable input with all mandatory 3D formats of HDMI 1.4a and many optional ones, up to UXGA at 8 bit (162.5 MHz TMDS clock). A programmable equalizer offsets cable loss at high frequencies and supports cables up to 30 m. HDCP 1.4 authentication, decryption and re-authentication run with keys stored on chip; repeater mode handles up to 127 KSVs. EDID is held in internal RAM. TERC4 error detection flags packets corrupted when a cable is pulled. The 5 V detect and Hot Plug assert pins are dedicated to the port. A CEC 1.4-compatible controller with the CDC feature is built in.
A regeneration block rebuilds DE from a measurement of the incoming format and filters HS and VS against glitches. HS, VS, FIELD and DE have programmable position, polarity and width.

Audio pulled from the HDMI stream leaves on AP as I2S (two channels) or S/PDIF (IEC 60958; two uncompressed channels or N compressed channels such as AC3), with a DST stream also available. Output can be LPCM or IEC 61937. A mute controller watches for conditions that would cause audible noise and ramps the audio down to avoid clicks and pops.

The component processor runs at up to 162.5 MHz and handles 525i, 625i, 525p, 625p, 720p, 1080i, 1080p and other formats. It provides contrast (gain), brightness (offset), hue and saturation adjustment, a free-run mode that keeps output timing steady with no input, standard identification (STDI), and decimation of RGB to 4:2:2 YCrCb. An any-to-any 3 × 3 colour space converter at its back end converts YPrPb to RGB, RGB to YCrCb, and between other colour spaces. DE is available to drive an HDMI/DVI transmitter directly.

The bus carries up to 24-bit 4:4:4 YCrCb. SDR mode gives 16- or 24-bit 4:2:2 or 24-bit 4:4:4; DDR mode gives 8- or 12-bit 4:2:2 YCrCb or 24-bit 4:4:4 RGB, up to 50 MHz. ITU-R BT.656 formats can carry embedded time codes alongside or instead of the HS, VS and FIELD pins. Bus rotation is supported, and every mode is chosen over I2C (OP_FORMAT_SEL).
The device is set up over I2C at up to 400 kHz. After reset the main map answers at 0x98. With a pull-up on VS/FIELD/ALSB and the SAMPLE_ALSB command issued, the address moves to 0x9A.
Two interrupt outputs. INT1 has its own pin. INT2 can be routed to one pin only, chosen from MCLK/INT2, SCLK/INT2 and HPA_A/INT2.
RESET is active low and must be held low at least 5 ms. Keep it low while the supplies come up. Power-up time is 25 ms typical.

Preferred order: bring up the 3.3 V supplies (DVDDIO, TVDD) first, then the 1.8 V supplies (DVDD, PVDD, CVDD). All supplies may instead rise together, provided no lower-voltage supply ever rises above a higher-voltage one while they settle.
All supplies may fall together, provided no higher-voltage supply drops below a lower-voltage one. A low-power power-down mode is available; switching off unused sections lowers dissipation.
The reference is a 28.63636 MHz crystal across XTALP and XTALN, ±50 ppm, or a 1.8 V 28.63636 MHz oscillator into XTALP.
θJA varies with the copper of the board, so die temperature is best found from the measured package top temperature and ΨJT. Junction temperature must not exceed 125°C.
The exposed pad (pin 0) on the underside connects to ground. A two-layer PCB design is supported. The device is ESD sensitive.
